mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-over-week acceleration in RETAIL_REC's own decline, from -24.0 to -68.3, reflects momentum in short-run retail demand suppression that will extrapolate forward, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks absent a reversal signal.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers by more than 25 points within the first two weeks of the forecast horizon, contradicting pure momentum extrapolation.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week collapse in WORKPLACES exceeding 25 percentage points, from -19.9 to -48.9, signals onset of a formal stay-at-home order. Such mandates historically persist at least two weeks before any easing, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed through that window.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 29 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the first two forecast weeks rises more than 15 points relative to t-0w despite the WORKPLACES threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous collapse of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES removes both the means and the occasion for discretionary retail trips. Their joint decline compounds to produce an outsized near-term drop in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -70.9 and WORKPLACES at -48.9 in same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the next week even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -40 points, indicating no compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: The steep PARKS decline from +17.9 to -51.4 is too abrupt to reflect normal seasonal drift and instead indicates an overriding policy closure; if the underlying regime is seasonal rather than mandated, PARKS and related outdoor-linked retail activity should rebound as conditions normalize, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40 points while no corroborating policy signal is present
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from +17.9 to -51.4 within three weeks
regime_hint: seasonal transition regime, not sustained lockdown
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -40 for the full four-week forecast horizon without rebound, indicating a non-seasonal (policy) cause and falsifying the seasonal rebound mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility rising above +20 points indicates near-saturation of stay-at-home behavior. Historical patterns show RETAIL_REC stabilizes rather than continuing to fall once RESIDENTIAL reaches this ceiling, as households hit a behavioral floor within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls more than 10 additional points over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +20, contradicting the saturation-stabilization claim.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous collapse across TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, PARKS, and RETAIL_REC at t-0w indicates a coordinated government lockdown. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC remains suppressed or declines further for the entire four-week forecast window until explicit policy easing signals appear.
evidence_refs: fact:all four categories fell sharply in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the t-0w level by more than 20 points within the first two weeks, indicating premature reopening not captured by the regime assumption.

mechanism_narrative: The rapid rise in RESIDENTIAL signals heightened household risk-aversion. This behavioral shift leads consumers to minimize non-essential outings, producing continued suppression of RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week regardless of policy announcements.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose steadily from 0.0 to 23.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 points in the week immediately following despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +20, contradicting the risk-aversion mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The combined sharp declines in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM suggest a weather-driven reduction in outdoor and errand activity that compounds with concurrent restrictions, producing a reinforcing negative effect on RETAIL_REC stronger than either factor alone over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -51.4 and GROCERY_PHARM fell to -26.7 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises despite continued joint decline in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM, indicating no compounding seasonal-behavioral effect.
